claim: Ventura County election officials are reducing voting locations in order to limit in-person voter turnout.

rows.answer: Yes, Ventura County officials significantly reduced the number of physical polling places for the November 2020 election compared to the March primary, implementing a new voting center model. The new model is also presented as offering greater flexibility, as voters are no longer assigned to a specific location based on their home address. As public information officer Miranda Nobriga explained, "There will be in-person locations but we are trying to stress to folks that those are for those who need that option."

rows.answer: Based on the search result, there is no official statement from Ventura County election officials explicitly stating that the reduction in voting locations is intended to limit in-person voter turnout. Public information officer Miranda Nobriga explained that "we are trying to stress to folks that those are for those who need that option," referring to in-person locations as an accommodation for those unable to vote by mail. The reduction from 389 polling places to 47 in-person locations was presented as part of a broader move to encourage vote-by-mail for public health reasons, with officials noting that more than 60% of registered voters had already been voting by mail in prior elections.
